summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and as Professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 2002 to 2008.

François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon and under Pierre Meile and Jean Filliozat. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1977 to 2002.
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. His appointments include serving as a professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2008 and 2013.

François Martini (1895–1965) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at INALCO under Sylvain Lévi, later serving as General Secretary of the Buddhist Institute (ca. 1930–1938) and working at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (ca. 1957–1965).
François-Marie Bertrand (1807–1881) was a scholar in the field of Indology. He studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice and under Garcin de Tassy.

Françoise L'Hernault (1937–1999) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at INALCO, Annamalai University, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and managed photographic collections at the École française d'Extrême-Orient beginning in 1971.

Françoise Mallison is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She succeeded Vaudeville in 1988 as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. She served as Director of Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine and as Director of Research at the CNRS.

Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She served as a director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental head roles at INALCO between 2011 and 2014.

Fred Henry Andrews (1866–1957) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was vice-principal at the National College of Arts (1890), Lahore Museum curator (ca. 1890–1899), and principal of Sri Pratap Technical College (1914).

Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Amherst College and Stanford University, and he taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (circa 1983–2005).

Fred Walter Householder, Jr. (1918–1994) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Columbia University under Louis H. Gray. He later served as Acting Chairman of Linguistics at Indiana University Bloomington (1948–1983).

Freda Bedi (1911–1977) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College and under Mahasi Sayadaw in 1953, and she founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

Frede Møller-Kristensen (1933–2003) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He lectured in Pāli at the University of Copenhagen (1966–1972) and directed the Oriental Department of the Royal Danish Library (1969–1987).

Frederic Salmon Growse (1836–1893) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Oriel College and The Queen's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1891 and was a Fellow of the University of Calcutta.
Frederic Spring was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society and was a Chaplain in the Madras Army until 1824.

Frederick Eden Pargiter (1852–1927) was an Indologist who studied at Exeter College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (ca. 1875–1904), as a Calcutta High Court judge (1904–1906), and as President of The Asiatic Society (1903–1905).

Frederick J. Streng (1933–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Texas Lutheran, SMU, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later teaching at USC and SMU.

Frederick James Furnivall (1825–1910) was a linguist educated at University College London and Trinity Hall. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), editor of the Oxford English Dictionary (1861–1870), and taught at the Working Men's College.
